solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Firm suffering setback — a coin is tossed to determine what happens

indicators.note: a setback sends the firm's letters going backwards

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: a tossed coin is flipped about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: 'is' shortens to 's, as in it's, giving S

explanation.surface: Some company down on its luck leaves its fate to the toss of a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' turns CO into OC; 'tossed' shuffles A COIN with S (the 's of 'is') into CASION.
explanation.definitionFit: An event or happening is something that takes place, so 'what happens' fits.

clue.text: Worry about identifying mark in the transport business

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the worry word goes round the mark

parts.note: to care is to worry or be anxious
a tag is a label that identifies something

explanation.surface: Someone frets over labelling goods in a haulage firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry' looks like the definition but is the outer word, wrapped 'about' the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage of goods by cart or lorry, and the charge for it, is the haulage trade.

clue.text: Assistants in a team when team's leader declines

indicators.note: in a down entry, to decline is to sink lower, so the leading letter drops to the bottom

parts.note: a side is a team, as in football
the first letter of the word for team

explanation.surface: Helpers in a squad find things going downhill when their captain loses form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team' is SIDE, so its leader is S; 'declines' moves that S from near the top of A SIDE down to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aides are helpers or assistants to someone senior.

clue.text: Naughty sister, about ten, aroused concerns

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are made to behave badly and get jumbled
about here means all around, the letters scattered about

explanation.surface: A mischievous girl of around ten makes everyone worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' and 'about' together shuffle SISTER and TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: One's interests are matters that arouse attention or concern, those things that engage curiosity.

clue.text: Established practices limiting an army of invaders?

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on both sides, so the practices go around the next word

parts.note: norms are established standards or practices

explanation.surface: Customs hem in an invading force.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as one example: an army of invaders, as in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The followers of William the Conqueror invaded England in 1066, an example of invaders.

clue.text: Work involved in separate sort of design

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so the work goes inside the separating word

parts.note: to part is to separate
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone's job is to keep apart different kinds of design.
explanation.walkthrough: OP (opus) is the standard crossword abbreviation for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s movement of Warhol and Lichtenstein produced a recognisable style of design and imagery.

clue.text: Hidden agent offering cannabis maybe

definitions.meaning: a spy or informer placed secretly inside an organisation
cannabis is one example of a growing herb or shrub

explanation.surface: A secret operative supplies drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mole inserted into a group and any growing vegetable organism, such as cannabis.

clue.text: Prince is a peculiar pedant

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the letters are made into an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: A royal heir turns out to be a fussy stickler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges PRINCE IS A.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler for exact rules and forms, a punctilious person, is a pedant.

clue.text: Tot playing in gang becoming bad

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled small child goes within the gang

parts.note: a ring is a gang, as in a drugs ring

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A toddler hanging around with a gang is going to the bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' jumbles TOT into OTT before 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaying, going off or putrefying is turning bad.

clue.text: What could be construed as direct approval

indicators.note: construed means interpreted, so the letters are read in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Something that might be taken as a straight thumbs-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could be construed as' rearranges DIRECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone recognition or praise for something is approval of it.

clue.text: Chemicals are abused by fellows

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: gents are gentlemen, fellows

explanation.surface: Some men misuse dangerous substances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges ARE into REA, followed by GENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Substances used in laboratory tests to produce a reaction are laboratory chemicals.

clue.text: Lackey in minister's house, right? Very short worker

parts.note: a manse is the house of a (chiefly Presbyterian) minister
very shortened to its abbreviation V
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A servant in the vicar's home, perhaps, who is a very small labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very short' is V, the abbreviation of very.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a male household servant, a valet or footman.

clue.text: Girl a bit of a looker

definitions.meaning: part of the eye, the coloured ring round the pupil, so a bit of something that looks

explanation.surface: A girl who is rather attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a looker' seems to be a pretty person, but it is an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female name and the pigmented part of the eye, an organ that looks.

clue.text: Deity in another mess

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A god finds himself in yet another muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters inside anotHER MESs.
explanation.definitionFit: The messenger god of Greek mythology is a deity.

clue.text: I am a helpful sort as Bradman now and then

definitions.text: I am a helpful sort as Bradman now and then

parts.words: I am a helpful sort as Bradman now and then
parts.note: the setter Bradman speaks; he is a man, and appears some weeks on the FT's Friday slot, so now and then he is a man of that weekday, which is also a willing helper

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being a useful fellow some of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradman is this puzzle's setter. The phrase for a devoted assistant (from Robinson Crusoe) also describes a male setter on a Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusoe's loyal servant gave his name to any trusty male assistant or helper.

clue.text: Session that could be of a standing committee!

definitions.text: Session that could be of a standing committee!

parts.words: Session that could be of a standing committee!
parts.note: a standing committee is a permanent one, but its meeting is a session when members are seated

explanation.surface: A meeting of a permanent committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' means permanent here, yet the meeting itself has the members seated.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting or session of a body such as Parliament or a court is a formal session.

clue.text: No!, we shout, when this building is demolished

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the letters are pulled apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Protesters cry out as a building is torn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is demolished' rearranges NO WE SHOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A terraced house in a city, or a family's urban home, is a type of building.

clue.text: Bishop with responsibilities and benefits

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an onus is a burden or responsibility; plural here

explanation.surface: A churchman with duties also gets perks.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra payments or advantages are benefits.

clue.text: Strange business — police activity with street sealed off

parts.note: biz is slang for business, as in showbiz

indicators.note: sealed off means shut out, so the street's abbreviation is removed from the police word

parts.note: making an arrest is what the police do

explanation.surface: An odd event: police close off a road during an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealed off' removes ST from ARREST, leaving ARRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird or odd things are strange.

clue.text: Corner of England has given up, withdrawn

parts.note: SE, the south-east, is a corner of England
ceded means surrendered or given up

explanation.surface: A region of England has surrendered and pulled out.
explanation.definitionFit: A state that has formally broken away from a union has withdrawn from it.

clue.text: Immoral person with need to get on

parts.note: to want is to need

explanation.surface: Someone loose-living is eager to make progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A promiscuous or dissolute person, as a noun, is an immoral person.

clue.text: Senior citizen strolled with difficulty, left to wander off

indicators.note: something done with difficulty is awkward, so these letters are moved into a new order
wander off means go away, so this letter leaves the walking word

explanation.surface: An elderly person walked unsteadily and was then left to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wander off' takes one L out of STROLLED, then 'with difficulty' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An old person, an elderly pensioner, is a senior citizen.

clue.text: Ruler, the last character to be see in limo?

indicators.note: to be seen in a vehicle means sitting inside it, so the letter goes within the car (see is presumably a slip for seen)

parts.note: a limousine is a car
Z is the last character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Would a monarch be the very last person to be spotted in a stretch limousine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be see in' places Z inside CAR; 'see' reads as a typo for 'seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor of Russia was an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: A cider's bad — tea should be drunk, something sugary

indicators.note: drunk means swallowed, so the tea goes inside the other letters
bad cider has gone off, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: The cider is off, so tea had better be drunk instead of something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges A CIDER'S into SAC-RIDE, and 'should be drunk' puts CHA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar, chemically, is a carbohydrate of this type, so it is something sugary.

clue.text: Method for joining opposites being demonstrated

indicators.note: joining here means linking the two compass letters by sitting between them

parts.note: S and N, south and north, are opposite compass points
how means the way or method

explanation.surface: A technique for uniting contrasts is on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for joining' sets HOW between the opposite compass points S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something displayed or exhibited is being demonstrated.

clue.text: Soldier exercising before line is put to flight

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A soldier drilling in front of the ranks is driven off.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive back an attacker, forcing them to flee, is to put to flight.

clue.text: Awfully drab car in northern city

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so these letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: A terribly dull vehicle seen in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' turns DRAB into BRAD, followed by FORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in West Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Arrogant at university when met with shame

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
'it's a shame' means 'it's a pity'

explanation.surface: A conceited student is met with disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means at university in British usage, as in going up to Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-important or presumptuous people are arrogant.

clue.text: African songstress entertained by king regularly

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is inside their house, so the singer goes inside
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: Enya is an Irish singer

explanation.surface: A female singer performs for a monarch on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes K and N from 'king'; 'entertained by' puts ENYA between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the East African nation is an African.

clue.text: End of road with Sam's family maybe? People in a neighbourhood

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens, so his family are the Wellers

explanation.surface: At the end of the road live Sam and his family, perhaps local folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Weller and his father Tony are characters in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents or inhabitants of a district are the people living there.
